extracted.intended_audience: tenants and landlords subject to the 1947 Housing and Rent Act; general newspaper readers seeking guidance on rent control rules
extracted.subtask_description: A newspaper-published Q&A and explanatory guidance about the 1947 Housing and Rent Act and rent-control administration (lease increases, filing/registration, eviction, decontrol, rent advisory boards, remedies). Targeted at landlords, tenants, and local rent-office administrators.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition of base/maximum rent
rubrics_metrics.description: The base rent is 'the maximum rent in effect on June 30, 1947, as modified by any subsequent order of the Rent Director.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Used as the starting point to determine allowable increases under the Act.

rubrics_metrics.name: 15% rent increase permitted by written lease
rubrics_metrics.description: A landlord may increase his rent by not more than 15 percent by voluntarily entering into a written lease expiring on or after December 31, 1948, provided he complies with filing requirements.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Increase is tied to a voluntary written lease meeting the expiration-date criterion and timely registration; if filing requirements are not met the lease does not change the maximum rent.

rubrics_metrics.name: Oral agreements do not change maximum rent
rubrics_metrics.description: No increase in the maximum rent of the unit is permissible based on an oral agreement; there must be the voluntary signing of a written lease.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Oral agreements are ineffective to alter the statutory maximum rent.

rubrics_metrics.name: Lease registration / filing requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: A copy of the lease and three copies of the registration of lease must be filed with the Area Rent Office within fifteen days after its date of execution.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If this is not done, the lease does not change the maximum rent. Registration forms are available at area rent offices.

rubrics_metrics.name: Effective date of new rent tied to filing compliance
rubrics_metrics.description: The new rent in a lease is effective on the lease's effective date provided the landlord meets the requirements of the Act and files the lease and registration copies with the Area Rent Office within fifteen days after execution.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Timely filing makes the lease's rent effective; failure to file timely negates the change to maximum rent.

rubrics_metrics.name: Area Rent Office does not issue order increasing maximum rent for new leases
rubrics_metrics.description: The Area Rent Office does not issue an order increasing the maximum rent as provided in a new lease.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The mechanism for a lease-based increase is the landlord/tenant written lease plus registration filing rather than a rent-office order increasing the maximum rent.

rubrics_metrics.name: Increase amount cannot exceed 15% (may be less)
rubrics_metrics.description: The increase provided for in the lease may not be more than 15 percent but it may be any lesser amount.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Landlords cannot use leases to obtain increases larger than the statutory cap.

rubrics_metrics.name: Base rent for calculating increase
rubrics_metrics.description: The base rent to which the rent increase provided for in the lease is added is the maximum rent in effect immediately prior to the effective date of the lease.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the immediately prior maximum rent as the reference point when applying the 15% (or lesser) increase.

rubrics_metrics.name: No retroactive change of maximum rent by Rent Office after a valid lease (includes hardship)
rubrics_metrics.description: The maximum rent established by a valid lease cannot be changed by order of the Rent Office; this includes hardship cases.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Once a valid lease sets the maximum rent, the Rent Office cannot later alter that maximum by order to increase or change it, even for hardship.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prohibition on lease provisions that decrease essential services to evade the Act
rubrics_metrics.description: A lease must not contain a provision decreasing the essential services, furniture, furnishings and equipment otherwise required by the regulation prior to the execution of the lease or decreasing other services, furniture, furnishings and equipment to a degree substantially less than that required by the regulation prior to the execution of the lease.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Leases cannot lawfully strip services or amenities to circumvent rent-regulation protections.

rubrics_metrics.name: Tenant option provisions allowed
rubrics_metrics.description: A lease may contain an option on the part of the tenant to terminate the lease prior to the expiration date of the lease.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Tenant termination options are permissible under the Act.

rubrics_metrics.name: Landlord unilateral termination option prohibited
rubrics_metrics.description: A lease may not contain an option on the part of the landlord to terminate the lease at will.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Clauses giving the landlord an option to terminate at will are invalid under the Act.

rubrics_metrics.name: Lease provisions intended to circumvent the Act are invalid
rubrics_metrics.description: Provisions in a lease that clearly have the intent of circumventing or evading the purposes of the Act (example given: clause terminating lease if tenant fails to keep garbage pail two feet two inches from fence) are invalid.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Courts/administrators will treat such evasion clauses as void.

rubrics_metrics.name: Eviction requires local-court proceedings and proof of statutory ground
rubrics_metrics.description: If a landlord notifies a tenant to vacate a dwelling unit, the landlord must go into a local court and prove that he has ground for such action under Section 209(a) of the Housing and Rent Act of 1947.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Landlords cannot rely solely on notice; proper judicial process is required; local waiting periods and court determinations will apply.

rubrics_metrics.name: Remedies for tenant overcharge
rubrics_metrics.description: If a tenant is overcharged, the tenant may bring an independent civil suit for recovery; remedies include treble damages or $50 whichever is greater, plus costs and reasonable attorney's fees.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Statutory civil remedies (including treble damages) are available to tenants harmed by overcharges.

rubrics_metrics.name: Decontrol — categories of accommodations eligible
rubrics_metrics.description: Certain types of accommodations are eligible for decontrol on and after specified dates, including (as listed) tourist homes serving ..., units not rented between Feb. 1, 1945 and Jan. ..., accommodations in hotels and other establishments except certain units, and all self-contained dwelling units (including kitchen and bath) in establishments in which the total number of self-contained dwelling units rented on June 30, 1947 ...
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Q&A enumerates categories and exceptions; eligibility for decontrol depends on the specific type and rental history of the accommodation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition of 'conversion' for decontrol purposes
rubrics_metrics.description: 'Conversion' means either a change in a structure from a non-housing use to a housing use or a structural change in a residential unit involving substantial alterations or remodeling and resulting in ...
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Conversion triggers particular decontrol and procedural rules; substantial structural change qualifies as conversion.

rubrics_metrics.name: Procedure and timing for securing decontrol
rubrics_metrics.description: Questions and guidance address the proper procedure for securing decontrol of accommodations and whether accommodations are decontrolled as of July 1, 1947 or at other dates.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Decontrol status depends on meeting specified conditions and on filing/administrative procedures described in the Act and regulations; rent control was extended until February 29, 1948 in some contexts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rent Advisory Board appointment and composition
rubrics_metrics.description: A Rent Advisory Board is appointed by the Housing Expediter from recommendations made by the respective ... (local authorities). There will initially be at least one board of less than five members for each defense-rental area.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Boards are local, small, and appointed via the Housing Expediter based on local recommendations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Functions of Rent Advisory Board
rubrics_metrics.description: The Board will consider cases presented by either landlord or tenant which it deems worthy of consideration and will make recommendations for their disposal to the Area Rent Director. The Board will also make recommendations directly to the Housing Expediter on (a) decontrol of the defense-rental area or any portion thereof, (b) the adequacy of the general rent level in the area, and (c) operations generally of the local rent office, with particular reference to hardship cases.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Boards are advisory; their remit includes case review, decontrol advice, rent-level adequacy, and operational recommendations focusing on hardship.

rubrics_metrics.name: Acceptability condition for Board recommendations
rubrics_metrics.description: In order to be acceptable the Board's recommendations must be in accordance with the Act and Rent Regulations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recommendations conflicting with statute or regulations will not be accepted.

rubrics_metrics.name: Eviction for purchaser's immediate personal use (good-faith requirement)
rubrics_metrics.description: A landlord (or purchaser) may proceed in a local court to evict a tenant if he seeks in good faith possession of the housing accommodations for his immediate and personal use and occupancy.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Eviction for conversion or purchaser-occupancy requires good-faith, immediate personal-use intent and must be proven in court; canned or bad-faith pretexts will be challenged.
